title: Purification of mouse hepatic non-parenchymal cells or nuclei for use in ChIP-seq and other next-generation sequencing approaches
protocol: Prepare necessary buffers and reagents.
Perform mouse dissection and liver digestion to generate a single-cell suspension enriched for liver non-parenchymal cells.
Immunolabel the generated cells for fluorescence-activated cell sorting (FACS).
Dilute a 10 mM aliquot of flavopiridol stock to 1 mM using water.
Store the 1 mM flavopiridol solution on ice.
Discard the 1 mM flavopiridol solution at the end of the day.
Prepare wash buffer 1 for use at 4°C or on ice.
Discard wash buffer 1 at the end of the day.
Prepare wash buffer 2 for use at 4°C or on ice.
Store wash buffer 2 for up to 1 week.
Discard wash buffer 2 after 1 week.
Mix 90% Percoll with 10% 10× Hank’s Balanced Salt Solution (no calcium, no magnesium, no phenol red) to make isotonic Percoll.
Store the isotonic Percoll solution on ice and discard at the end of the day.
Prepare Liberase TM (5 mg/mL) and store it on ice.
Do not vortex or vigorously pipette when preparing Liberase TM.
Immediately freeze unused Liberase TM enzyme at −80°C in single-use aliquots (1.25 mL per healthy mouse liver).
Mix collagenases with calcium-containing Hank’s Balanced Salt Solution to prepare Liver digestion buffer A.
Store and use the Liver digestion buffer A at 37°C.
Prepare Liver clearing buffer and store it at 37°C for use.
Prepare Liver digestion buffer B immediately prior to euthanizing a group of mice, using 60 mL per mouse or 80 mL if expected liver enlargement or disease.
Prepare OptiPrep by mixing the commercial iso-osmolar iodixanol solution before use.
Mix PBS and 0.1% Tween 20 to create a 50 mL solution for enzyme digestion purposes.
Flush blood from the liver of a freshly euthanized mouse according to institutional guidelines.
Pin down the mouse and carefully open its abdominal cavity.
Expose the inferior vena cava and portal vein by gently moving the intestines aside.
Insert a 24-gauge catheter into the inferior vena cava.
Attach the line of a peristalsis pump connected to a 0.22-μm filter to the catheter.
Pin the lines in place at the filter after nicking the portal vein with scissors and releasing fluid pressure.
Close the inferior vena cava above the diaphragm using a bulldog clamp.
Apply a slight vacuum using a 1 mL syringe if necessary to fill the catheter hub with blood.
Secure the catheter and peristalsis lines by pinning the filter in place on the dissection mount.
Maintain liver temperature at around 37°C using a heat lamp.
Perfuse liver tissue with liver clearing buffer for 3 min at a flow rate of 5 mL/min.
Move the pump intake line to a tube with 40 mL of liver digestion buffer B.
Allow the contents to perfuse through the liver until the line is empty.
Remove the gallbladder using scissors and tweezers.
Continue digesting liver tissue in vitro.
Aspirate the digested liver into a 1 mL syringe or remove lobes with scissors and forceps, then finely mince the tissue using a razor blade.
Transfer the digested contents into a 50 mL conical tube filled with 20 mL of liver digestion buffer B.
Mix the digested liver tissue with digestion buffer by pipetting up and down 3–5 times or by gently inverting the tubes.
Incubate the digested liver tissue for 20 min at 37°C on a Miltenyi MACSmix tube rotator at the highest speed.
Remove hepatocytes from the cell suspension by low-speed centrifugation followed by Percoll centrifugation.
Centrifuge liver suspension at 500 × g for 10 min at 4°C to pellet non-parenchymal cells if the liver is healthy and non-steatotic.
Filter 20 mL of cells suspended in liver digestion buffer through a 70 μm cell strainer into a 50 mL conical tube to remove undigested debris and connective tissue.
Add 20 mL of wash buffer 1 to dilute liver digestion buffer and slow enzymatic activity during hepatocyte removal.
Sediment dense hepatocytes by low-speed centrifugation at 50 × g for 3 min at 4°C.
Transfer the supernatant to a new 50 mL conical tube and repeat spin at 50 × g for 3 min at 4°C, discarding the pellet containing hepatocytes.
Add 10 ml isotonic Percoll to 40 ml cell suspension and centrifuge in 20% Percoll at 600 × g for 10 min at 4°C if isolating non-parenchymal cells (NPCs) using a Percoll wash.
Remove supernatant after centrifugation with isotonic Percoll and resuspend NPCs in 20 ml of wash buffer 1.
Centrifuge the NPC cell suspension at 500 × g for 10 min at 4°C to pellet NPCs once more.
Resuspend pellet in 10 mL of OptiPrep (28%) using a 10 mL syringe with an 18-gauge needle attached.
Transfer the 10 mL cell suspension in OptiPrep buffer through the Pasteur pipette to create the cell layer underneath the less dense wash buffer 1 layer.
Centrifuge gradient suspension at 1,400 × g for 25 min at 4°C with centrifuge acceleration set to very low and with brake mechanism turned off.
Following gradient centrifugation, extract all cells at the interface between the upper 0% OptiPrep layer and the lower 28% OptiPrep layer using a 1 mL pipette tip.
Transfer the extracted cell mixture to a new 15 mL conical tube and fill it with wash buffer 2 up to 12 mL.
Resuspend red blood cells remaining in non-parenchymal cell mixture in 1 mL of RBC lysis buffer at 4°C, incubate for 5 min on ice.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 500 × g for 10 min at 4°C.
Remove supernatant and resuspend the cells in 1 mL of PBS at 4°C.
Pellet NPCs via centrifugation at 400 × g for 7 min at 4°C.
Remove the supernatant and wash the cells with 10 mL of PBS at 4°C.
Stain non-parenchymal cells with viability dye.
Set aside some unstained cells to determine background fluorescence.
Centrifuge cell suspension at 500 × g for 10 min at 4°C.
Resuspend cell pellet in 250 to 500 μL of PBS containing anti-CD16/CD32 and Live/Dead NIR Viability Dye or similar.
Stain at 4°C for 10 minutes.
Freshly prepare 250 to 500 μL of the antibody staining cocktail per liver.
Add an equivalent volume used in step 8b of the 2× antibody staining cocktail to the cells.
Mix together by inversion 20 times or using gentle flicking.
Stain at 4°C for 20 minutes.
Fill the tube with wash buffer 2 at the end of the staining process.
Pellet the NPCs by centrifugation at 500 × g for 10 minutes at 4°C.
Remove the supernatant.
Resuspend pellet in 2 mL wash buffer 2.
Filter the cells through a 35- or 40-μm cell strainer to remove particulate matter that may clog the cell sorter.
Flush the strainer with wash buffer 2.
Fill the tube with wash buffer 2.
Pellet the non-parenchymal cell suspension at 500 × g for 10 minutes at 4°C.
Remove supernatant.
Resuspend in 500 μL wash buffer 2.
Keep the cells on ice and in the dark (covered).
Cells are now ready for FACS.
Sort the stained single-cell suspension into purified cell populations using FACS.
Prepare single-color controls using compensation beads from Invitrogen.
Mix 1–2 μg of antibody per compensation control to ensure a fluorescent signal higher than that of stained cells.
Set a gating strategy for Kupffer cells based on expression levels of Tim4.
Generate a dot plot of CD45 versus CD146.
Set gates for CD146−CD45+ immune cells.
Set gates for CD146+CD45− endothelial cells.
Generate a dot plot of CD11b versus F4/80 for the CD146−CD45+ population identified in step 20a.
Set gate for CD11bloF4/80hi tissue macrophages.
Generate a dot plot of side scatter pulse height versus side scatter pulse area to identify single cells and exclude doublets.
Generate a dot plot of forward scatter versus Zombie NIR to identify live cells and exclude dead cells.
Live cells will be Zombie NIR negative.
Use a fluorescence minus one control for Zombie NIR to define your viable cell gate.
Generate a dot plot of Tim4-A647.
Tim4+ cells are long-term resident or embryonic-derived Kupffer cells while Tim4− cells are monocyte-derived macrophages recruited during disease to the Kupffer cell niche.
Select the CD11bhiF4/80lo population displayed in step 11b.
Select CX3CR1+Ly6G− cells to exclude neutrophils.
Further divide selected cells based on expression of Ly6C into Ly6Clo recruited macrophages and Ly6Chi recruited macrophages.
Identify singlets.
Identify live cells.
Set gating strategy for liver sinusoidal endothelial cells.
Gate on CD146+CD45− cells to identify liver sinusoidal endothelial cells.
Generate a plot of retinoid autofluorescence versus side scatter to identify stellate cells.
Excite retinoid autofluorescent stellate cells with an ultraviolet (355 nm) laser.
Detect retinoid autofluorescence at approximately 500 nm.
Assess purity of sorted cells by flow cytometry using a small number of sorted cells diluted in wash buffer.
Prepare sorted viable cells for ChIP-seq.
Start with 0.5 to 1 million cells for ChIP-seq library preparation.
For Kupffer cells, use 1–3 livers to obtain the required number of cells.
For sinusoidal endothelial cells, use 1 liver to obtain the required number of cells.
Other populations of non-parenchymal cells may require testing to determine necessary sample size.
Wash the desired number of cells with wash buffer 2.
Centrifuge the cells at 500 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Remove the supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 500 μL wash buffer 2.
Transfer to a 1.5 mL DNA LoBind tube.
Wash the starting tube with an additional 500 μL wash buffer 2.
Combine into the 1.5 mL DNA LoBind tube.
Centrifuge the cells in the 1.5 mL DNA LoBind tube at 500 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Resuspend the pellet in 1% formaldehyde at 20°C–25°C, using approximately 1 million cells per mL.
Incubate for 10 min at 20°C–25°C with gentle rocking or rotation to cross-link proteins and DNA.
Quench the cross-linking reaction by adding glycine to a final concentration of 0.125 M from a 2.625 M stock solution.
Add Tween 20 to a final concentration of 0.1% from a 10% stock solution.
Centrifuge the cross-linked cells at 800 × g for 10 min at 4°C.
Confirm the presence of a cell pellet.
If no pellet is apparent, centrifuge again at 1,200 × g for 10 min at 4°C.
Aspirate the supernatant carefully to avoid disturbing the cell pellet.
Suspend the cross-linked cells in 1 mL PBS + 0.1% Tween 20 at 4°C.
Centrifuge at 800–1,200 × g for 10 min at 4°C.
Aspirate the supernatant carefully to avoid disturbing the cell pellet.
Wash the cells once more by repeating step 29.
Centrifuge the sample for a few seconds at 800–1,200 × g.
Aspirate as much residual supernatant as possible using a p10 pipette tip.
Be very careful to avoid disturbing the cell pellet.
Snap-freeze the pellet using liquid nitrogen.
Store the cross-linked cells at -80°C until ready for ChIP-seq library preparation.
Alternatively, snap-freeze the samples using an alcohol and dry ice bath.
Take care to protect the tube labeling.
Prepare liver clearing buffer for each mouse liver.
Dissolve 100 mg vials of DSG using 4 mL of DMSO.
Rapidly dispense the DSG/DMSO solution into 176 ml of PBS and mix by inverting 5-6 times.
Keep the diluted DSG solution at 20°C–25°C until use.
Dilute stock formaldehyde solution to 1% volume/volume using 20°C–25°C PBS.
Keep diluted formaldehyde at 20°C–25°C until use.
Dilute 1.9 ml of 2.625 M stock glycine into 18.1 ml 20°C–25°C PBS to prepare 20 mL 0.25 M glycine solution.
Chill and use nuclei isolation buffer on ice.
Chill and use nuclei sorting buffer on ice.
Flush blood from the liver of a freshly euthanized mouse following institutional approved guidelines.
Pin down the mouse.
Carefully open the abdominal cavity.
Gently move the intestines to expose the inferior vena cava and portal vein.
Insert a 24-gauge catheter into the inferior vena cava.
Attach the line of a peristalsis pump connected to a 0.22-μm filter to the catheter and pin it into place.
Nick the portal vein with scissors to release fluid pressure.
Close the inferior vena cava above the diaphragm using a bulldog clamp.
If the liver does not blanch, adjust the position of the catheter in the vessel carefully.
Apply surgical glue or use a suture to secure the catheter in place.
Perfuse 20°C–25°C Liver clearing buffer 2 at 5 mL/min for 3 min.
Switch the perfusion line to a solution of 1 mg/mL DSG prepared in 20°C–25°C phosphate buffered saline.
Perfuse for 30 min, which requires approximately 180 mL/mouse.
Switch the perfusion line to a solution containing 1% formaldehyde prepared in 20°C–25°C phosphate buffered saline.
Perfuse for 10 min, which requires approximately 60 mL per mouse.
Switch the perfusion line to a vessel containing 20 mL of 20°C–25°C 0.25 M glycine and allow the perfusion line to fully empty.
Homogenize the liver.
Remove the fixed liver and dispose of the hazardous mouse carcass following institutional guidelines.
Finely mince the liver with a razor in a 5 cm plastic dish, then transfer the minced tissue to a 50 mL conical tube.
Wash the liver twice by suspending in 20 mL nuclei isolation buffer and centrifuging for 1,200 × g for 7 min at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant after each wash.
Suspend the washed liver tissue in 15 mL nuclei isolation buffer then transfer to a 15 mL Dounce homogenizer.
Using the loose pestle, homogenize slowly 10 times with ¼ to ½ rotation on the downward stroke and no rotation on the upward stroke.
Incubate on ice for 30 min.
Using the tight pestle, homogenize slowly 10 times with ¼ to ½ rotation on the downward stroke and no rotation on the upward stroke.
Transfer the homogenate to a 15 mL conical tube.
Centrifuge the tube at 1,200 × g for 7 minutes at 4°C.
Resuspend the pellet in 10 mL of fresh nuclei isolation buffer.
Repeat steps 3 and 4 two to four times until the supernatant is clear.
Examine the nuclei under a microscope using trypan blue and a hemocytometer.
If cells are intact, repeat steps 41g–i as necessary.
Suspend the cleaned nuclei at approximately 20 million nuclei per mL.
Pause Point: Nuclei can be suspended in 10 mL of 90% FBS and 10% DMSO (per liver) and stored in aliquots at -80°C for later use.
To recover a cryopreserved sample, warm the frozen suspension at 37°C in a water bath.
Wash the nuclei twice with nuclei isolation buffer after thawing.
Save a small portion of the sample for use as an unstained control.
Add 1 μg/mL anti-CD16/CD32 to prevent nonspecific binding and incubate at 4°C for 20 min.
Add 1 μg/mL Alexa Fluor 647 conjugated anti-PU.1 and stain at 4°C for 30 min or overnight as optimized empirically.
Fill the tube with nuclei isolation buffer and centrifuge at 1,200 × g for 7 min at 4°C.
Aspirate the supernatant and refill the tube with nuclei isolation buffer.
Centrifuge again at 1,200 × g for 7 min at 4°C.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Suspend washed nuclei in nuclei sorting buffer.
Pass the suspension through a 22-gauge needle slowly.
Pass the suspension through a 40-μm cell strainer.
Store the suspended nuclei on ice until sorting.
Purify desired nuclei population using fluorescence-activated nuclei sorting.
Set up instrument detector thresholds and voltages/gains for light scatter.
Monitor droplet profile stability during sorting.
Monitor event rate stability during sorting.
Verify yield by microscopy after purification.
Verify purity by flow cytometry after purification.
Centrifuge nuclei at 800 to 1,200 × g for 10 min at 4°C in PBS + 0.01% Tween 20.
Aspirate all buffer carefully after centrifugation.
Quick spin the nuclei once more at 800 to 1,200 × g.
Remove all buffer without disturbing the nuclei pellet.
Snap-freeze the pellet using liquid nitrogen.
Store the snap-frozen pellet at −80°C until use for ChIP.
